**Frank-Walter Steinmeier** (German: [[ˈfʁaŋkˌvaltɐ ˈʃtaɪnˌmaɪ.ɐ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Standard_German "Help:IPA/Standard German") [ⓘ](/wiki/File:De-Frank-Walter_Steinmeier.ogg "File:De-Frank-Walter Steinmeier.ogg"); born 5 January 1956)[[1]](#cite_note-3) is a German politician who has served as [President of Germany](/wiki/President_of_Germany "President of Germany") since 2017.[[2]](#cite_note-4) He was previously [Minister for Foreign Affairs](/wiki/Minister_for_Foreign_Affairs_(Germany) "Minister for Foreign Affairs (Germany)") from 2005 to 2009 and again from 2013 to 2017, as well as [Vice-Chancellor of Germany](/wiki/Vice-Chancellor_of_Germany "Vice-Chancellor of Germany") from 2007 to 2009. Steinmeier was [Chairman-in-Office](/wiki/Chairman-in-Office "Chairman-in-Office") of the [Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe](/wiki/Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe "Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe") (OSCE) in 2016.

Steinmeier is a member of the [Social Democratic Party of Germany](/wiki/Social_Democratic_Party_of_Germany "Social Democratic Party of Germany") (SPD), holds a doctorate in law and was formerly a career civil servant. He was a close aide of [Gerhard Schröder](/wiki/Gerhard_Schr%C3%B6der "Gerhard Schröder") when Schröder was [Minister-President of Lower Saxony](/wiki/Minister-President_of_Lower_Saxony "Minister-President of Lower Saxony") during most of the 1990s, and served as Schröder's chief of staff from 1996. When Schröder became [Chancellor of Germany](/wiki/Chancellor_of_Germany "Chancellor of Germany") in 1998, Steinmeier was appointed Under-Secretary of State in the [German Chancellery](/wiki/German_Chancellery "German Chancellery") with responsibility for the [intelligence services](/wiki/Intelligence_service "Intelligence service"). Pakistan :: part 04 :: chunk_0003
**Pakistan**,[[f]](#cite_note-13) officially the **Islamic Republic of Pakistan**,[[g]](#cite_note-14) is a country in [South Asia](/wiki/South_Asia "South Asia"). It is the [fifth-most populous country](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population "List of countries and dependencies by population"), with a population of over 241.5 million,[[d]](#cite_note-fn3-10) having the [second-largest Muslim population](/wiki/Islam_by_country#Countries "Islam by country") as of 2023. [Islamabad](/wiki/Islamabad "Islamabad") is the nation's capital, while [Karachi](/wiki/Karachi "Karachi") is [its largest city](/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Pakistan_by_population "List of cities in Pakistan by population") and [financial centre](/wiki/Financial_centre "Financial centre"). Pakistan is the [33rd-largest country by area](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area "List of countries and dependencies by area"). Bounded by the [Arabian Sea](/wiki/Arabian_Sea "Arabian Sea") on the south, the [Gulf of Oman](/wiki/Gulf_of_Oman "Gulf of Oman") on the southwest, and the [Sir Creek](/wiki/Sir_Creek "Sir Creek") on the southeast, it shares land borders with [India](/wiki/India "India") to the east; [Afghanistan](/wiki/Afghanistan "Afghanistan") to the west; [Iran](/wiki/Iran "Iran") to the southwest; and [China](/wiki/China "China") to the northeast. It shares a maritime border with [Oman](/wiki/Oman "Oman") in the Gulf of Oman, and is separated from [Tajikistan](/wiki/Tajikistan "Tajikistan") in the northwest by Afghanistan's narrow [Wakhan Corridor](/wiki/Wakhan_Corridor "Wakhan Corridor").

Pakistan is the site of [several ancient cultures](/wiki/History_of_Pakistan "History of Pakistan"), including the 8,500-year-old [Neolithic](/wiki/Neolithic "Neolithic") site of [Mehrgarh](/wiki/Mehrgarh "Mehrgarh") in [Balochistan](/wiki/Balochistan,_Pakistan "Balochistan, Pakistan"), the [Indus Valley Civilisation](/wiki/Indus_Valley_Civilisation "Indus V

Lonzo Ball :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
As a senior at [Chino Hills High School](/wiki/Chino_Hills_High_School "Chino Hills High School") in 2016 Ball was awarded multiple national high school player of the year honors, and led his team, alongside his brothers [LiAngelo](/wiki/LiAngelo_Ball "LiAngelo Ball") and [LaMelo](/wiki/LaMelo_Ball "LaMelo Ball"), to an undefeated 35–0 record and the consensus national top ranking. As a college freshman in 2016–17, he led the nation in [assists](/wiki/Assist_(basketball) "Assist (basketball)") and broke the UCLA record for the most assists in a season. Ball also won the [Wayman Tisdale Award](/wiki/Wayman_Tisdale_Award "Wayman Tisdale Award") as the top freshman in the nation.

As an NBA rookie with the Lakers, his playing time was limited by shoulder and knee injuries, and he was sidelined for much of his second season after an ankle injury. He was traded at the end of the season to the [New Orleans Pelicans](/wiki/New_Orleans_Pelicans "New Orleans Pelicans") in a trade package for [Anthony Davis](/wiki/Anthony_Davis "Anthony Davis"). He played two seasons with the Pelicans before joining the [Chicago Bulls](/wiki/Chicago_Bulls "Chicago Bulls") in a [sign-and-trade deal](/wiki/Sign-and-trade_deal "Sign-and-trade deal"), but a persistent knee injury sidelined him for the majority of his tenure with the team, with him missing the entirety of the [2022–23](/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Chicago_Bulls_season "2022–23 Chicago Bulls season") and [2023–24 seasons](/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Chicago_Bulls_season "2023–24 Chicago Bulls season"). After the [2024–25](/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_Chicago_Bulls_season "2024–25 Chicago Bulls season") season, Ball was traded to the [Cleveland Cavaliers](/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers").

The State of New York has a primarily urban population. The largest city in the state is [New York City](/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), which is also one of the world's most ethnically diverse and cosmopolitan cities. Additional major urban centers include [Albany](/wiki/Albany,_New_York "Albany, New York"), [Buffalo](/wiki/Buffalo,_New_York "Buffalo, New York"), [Rochester](/wiki/Rochester,_New_York "Rochester, New York"), [Syracuse](/wiki/Syracuse,_New_York "Syracuse, New York") and [Utica](/wiki/Utica,_New_York "Utica, New York"). The state has 62 counties; the most populated one is [Kings County](/wiki/Kings_County,_New_York "Kings County, New York") ([Brooklyn](/wiki/Brooklyn,_New_York "Brooklyn, New York")). Much of New York State's population outside of New York City is concentrated in the [Long Island](/wiki/Long_Island "Long Island"), [Hudson Valley](/wiki/Hudson_Valley "Hudson Valley"), [Western New York](/wiki/Western_New_York "Western New York"), [Finger Lakes](/wiki/Finger_Lakes "Finger Lakes"), and [Capital District](/wiki/Capital_District_(New_York) "Capital District (New York)") regions; if the population of New York City is included, this amounts to 90% of the state's total population.

The intense development, urbanization and suburban sprawl of New York City makes it the most populated region in New York and the collective U.S., an estimated 20 to 30 million in the eight-state [Megalopolis](/wiki/Megalopolis_(city_type) "Megalopolis (city type)") stretching 500 miles from [Boston](/wiki/Boston "Boston") to [Washington, D.C.](/wiki/Washington,_D.C. Main article: [Supreme Court of the United States](/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States")

The Supreme Court was created by [Article III](/wiki/Article_Three_of_the_United_States_Constitution "Article Three of the United States Constitution") of the [United States Constitution](/wiki/Constitution_of_the_United_States "Constitution of the United States"), which stipulates that the "judicial power of the United States, shall be vested in one Supreme Court,"[[4]](#cite_note-4) and was organized by the [1st United States Congress](/wiki/1st_United_States_Congress "1st United States Congress"). Through the [Judiciary Act of 1789](/wiki/Judiciary_Act_of_1789 "Judiciary Act of 1789"), Congress specified the Court's [original](/wiki/Original_jurisdiction "Original jurisdiction") and [appellate jurisdiction](/wiki/Appellate_jurisdiction "Appellate jurisdiction"), created thirteen judicial districts, and fixed the number of justices at six (one chief justice and five associate justices).[[5]](#cite_note-5)[[6]](#cite_note-6)

Since 1789, Congress has occasionally altered the size of the Supreme Court, historically in response to the country's own expansion in size. An [1801 act](/wiki/Midnight_Judges_Act "Midnight Judges Act") would have decreased the Court's size to five members upon its next vacancy. However, an [1802 act](/wiki/Judiciary_Act_of_1802 "Judiciary Act of 1802") negated the effects of the 1801 act upon the Court before any such vacancy occurred, maintaining the Court's size at six members. Later legislation increased its size to [seven members in 1807](/wiki/Seventh_Circuit_Act_of_1807 "Seventh Circuit Act of 1807"), to [nine in 1837](/wiki/Eighth_and_Ninth_Circuits_Act_of_1837 "Eighth and Ninth Circuits Act of 1837"), and to [ten in 1863](/wiki/Tenth_Circuit_Act_of_1863 "Tenth Circuit Act of 1863"). White rhino hooves have three broad, distinct toes.

The white rhinoceros is the largest of the five living rhinoceros species and one of the largest [megafauna](/wiki/Megafauna "Megafauna") in existence. Judged by mean body mass, only the three extant species of [elephant](/wiki/Elephant "Elephant") surpass it.[[23]](#cite_note-24)[[24]](#cite_note-25) Though the body mass of individual rhinoceros often overlap with that of individual [hippopotamuses](/wiki/Hippopotamuses "Hippopotamuses"), with whom it shares a habitat, the white rhinoceros weighs more on average.[[25]](#cite_note-Piennar_etal_1966-26) The white rhino's mass is evident in its large, barrel-shaped body and its immense head, which are connected by a short, powerful neck.

Males (bulls) typically have a head-and-body length of 3.7–4 m (12.1–13.1 ft) and a shoulder height of 170–186 cm (5.58–6.10 ft), while females (cows) measure 3.35–3.65 m (11.0–12.0 ft) in head-and-body length and 160–177 cm (5.25–5.81 ft) at the shoulder.[[26]](#cite_note-Macdonald,_D._2001-27)[[27]](#cite_note-MS-28) The tail adds approximately 70 cm (28 in) to the total length. Bulls are heavier, averaging 2,000–2,300 kg

Main article: [Cradle of Liberty Council v. City of Philadelphia](/wiki/Cradle_of_Liberty_Council_v._City_of_Philadelphia "Cradle of Liberty Council v. City of Philadelphia")

On July 31, 2006, Mayor Street ordered the local [Boy Scouts](/wiki/Boy_Scouts_of_America "Boy Scouts of America") council, Cradle of Liberty Council, to admit [gay](/wiki/Homosexual "Homosexual") scout leaders, vacate the city-owned building that it has occupied since 1928, or pay market rent.[[29]](#cite_note-Inkysolicitor-29) Although the city subsidizes rental space for more than 75 community and activist organizations, including 14 other youth organizations and several religious groups that have restrictive membership policies, the Mayor took the position that the Boy Scouts were not in compliance with the city's anti-discrimination ordinance.[[29]](#cite_note-Inkysolicitor-29) The Scouts argued that the city's action violated their right to [freedom of assembly](/wiki/Freedom_of_assembly "Freedom of assembly") guaranteed under the [First Amendment to the United States Constitution](/wiki/First_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "First Amendment to the United States Constitution"). The case ended with the court ruling in favor of the Boy Scouts of America.[[30]](#cite_note-30)[[31]](#cite_note-31) The Cradle of Liberty Council was also awarded $877,000 for legal costs arising from the city's unlawful action.[[32]](#cite_note-philly.com-32)
